name: Matrix Scroller
author: Mike Neiderhauser
description: Scrolls song information and custom text across LED matrix panels using FPP's Overlay Model API. Per-panel config, per-song and per-sequence overrides, repeat delay, FPP commands, and a web UI. Can also drive a matrix on another FPP player you name. Includes a Home Assistant dashboard for remote control.

privacy.summary: Scrolls the playing song's title and artist, or your own text, across matrix models on this player. It talks only to FPP on this device unless you point it at another player.

sends.to: http://the FPP player you set as FPP Host (this device by default)
sends.what: requests for what is playing, and the text and colours to show
sends.why: to show scrolling text on a matrix attached to that player

systemChanges.what: runs a background program whenever FPP is running, which checks what is playing about once a second
its background program listens on 127.0.0.1:32329, reachable only from this device; FPP's web server passes requests to it
installs five playlist scripts (ms_*.sh) into media/scripts; uninstall removes them

privacy.other: Its API is served through FPP's web server, so anyone who can open this player's FPP pages can change its settings, set the text shown on the matrices, and turn its output on or off, the same as FPP itself; the optional Home Assistant files use that API. Its FPP commands do the same (panels on/off, messages, restoring a snapshot) from anything that can run FPP commands, including MQTT and other FPP players. It switches the overlay models you choose on and off to draw text. It writes an activity log (logs/plugin-fpp-matrixscroller.log); at debug level that includes the messages and song titles it shows. Its settings (config/plugin.fpp-matrixscroller.json) and saved snapshots (plugindata/fpp-matrixscroller/) stay after uninstall.
